calls.headline: Outside money buys EGX shares as locals sell into a 0.99% fall
calls.body: The EGX30 fell 0.99% to 51,681.60 on Tuesday and the EGX70 EWI 2.42% to 17,592.80, as 179 stocks fell and 31 rose on EGP 9.42bn of turnover (Al-Masdar, Masrawy). Arabs bought a net EGP 115m and foreigners EGP 79.5m in listed stocks, excluding deals, while Egyptians sold EGP 194.5m (Masrawy, Al Mal, Vetogate). The central bank's dollar rate held at EGP 53.80 on Wednesday morning, while the S&P 500 fell for a fourth day and the US 10-year yield stayed above 5%.
calls.view: The selling was local and broad, after a 7.7% small-cap run in the week to November 12, not an exit by outside money: Arabs and foreigners were net buyers on a day every S&P sector fell. With the pound steady and Nvidia's beat lifting US futures about 0.5%, the desk expects the blue chips to hold above 50,000 into MSCI's November 30 changes. Low confidence: there is no single trigger behind the selling to argue either way.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 49,500 before November 30.

calls.headline: Fertilizer gas costs 50% more, in return for full exports
calls.line: Abu Qir's disclosure confirms the new price runs from November 16 to December 31.
calls.body: Seven fertilizer producers agreed to pay $175m upfront for gas at $12.75 per mmBtu, up 50% from $8.50, for 45 days from November 16, in return for exporting all their output and a pause in supplying subsidized fertilizer; gas cuts of 20–40% stay (Asharq Business via EnterpriseAM). Abu Qir disclosed that its price changes under a new decree for November 16 to December 31 (Al-Borsa). EnterpriseAM puts Egyptian urea at about $535 a ton FOB. Abu Qir slipped 0.1% to EGP 77.05 and MOPCO 0.5% to EGP 38.84.
calls.view: At about 25 mmBtu a ton, the rise adds roughly $100 to the gas cost of each ton of urea, close to a fifth of its export price, so margins fall even though volumes recover. The desk keeps its view that fertilizer stocks stay under pressure through November, at low confidence: full exports at $535 urea still leave a profit, and Abu Qir trades well below the desk's EGP 85 line.
calls.wrong: Abu Qir closes above EGP 85 before November 30, or the cuts are lifted.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction's nine-month profit nearly doubles to $218m
calls.line: A record $11.6bn backlog, a week before 97.2m new shares list.
calls.body: Profit attributable to shareholders rose 95.9% to $218.0m in the nine months to September against an adjusted $111.3m, which leaves out a $22.0m gain from legal cases; on the reported base the rise is 63.5% (company release; Fintech Gate). Third-quarter profit rose 103% to $102.7m on revenue up 22.5% to $1.80bn, and the backlog is $11.6bn, $4.8bn of it in the US. The stock closed flat at EGP 815.10 before the release.
calls.view: Dollar earnings growing this fast in both the Gulf and the US put the stock at about 6 times earnings, cheap for a firm whose revenue is mostly in dollars. The 97.2m new shares for the OCI merger on November 24 are the near-term weight; the desk keeps its EGP 860–900 range by end of January, at low confidence.
calls.wrong: It closes below EGP 780, or the dollar falls below EGP 52.

calls.headline: EFG Holding's quarterly profit falls 15% as its lender lags
calls.line: EFG Hermes' revenue rose 36%, but EFG Finance's profit fell 43%.
calls.body: Profit after tax and minorities fell 15% to EGP 720m in the third quarter as revenue rose 5% to EGP 6.7bn, or 27% excluding one-off asset-sale gains at Banque Nextt a year earlier (Fintech Gate; Reuters headline via TradingView). EFG Hermes earned EGP 342m on revenue up 36% to EGP 2.9bn; EFG Finance's profit fell 43% to EGP 150m, and Banque Nextt contributed EGP 228m. The stock closed flat at EGP 24.09.
calls.view: The investment bank is earning from the busiest EGX turnover in a year and the state's offerings, and it runs Misr Life's 15% sale in December; the lending arm and higher taxes are the drag. The desk sees no case either way for the stock until the bank's margins show the October 29 hike, at low confidence.
calls.wrong: EFG Hermes' fee income falls in the fourth quarter despite the Misr Life offering.

calls.headline: Sisi says the IMF program is nearly done; the dollar holds at EGP 53.80
calls.line: A test for the carry trade as US yields stay above 5%.
calls.body: President Sisi said Egypt's IMF program is nearing completion, citing 5.1% growth last fiscal year and reserves of $57.5bn (Daily News Egypt, Egypt Today). The central bank's dollar rate held at 53.66 to buy and 53.80 to sell on Wednesday morning, within 1% of its strongest in a year. Abroad, the dollar index stood at 103.60, near its highest since April 2025, the US 10-year yield above 5% and futures price a December Fed hike (Reuters via AOL).
calls.view: Finishing the program before it expires on December 15 removes the main local risk to the pound; dearer US money is the outside one, and the carry still pays: the one-year bill yielded 26.07% at the November 12 auction against 5.1% on US 10-year debt. The desk keeps the pound firmer than EGP 56 into the IMF review, at medium confidence. Local gold, at EGP 5,900 for 21K, has yet to follow the ounce below $3,800.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9.

calls.headline: Nvidia beats with $115.8bn and guides to $130bn
calls.body: Nvidia's revenue rose 103% to $115.8bn in the quarter to October 25, against $109.1bn expected, with data-center revenue up 110% to $107.6bn; GAAP net income rose 105% to $65.3bn (SEC filing; BigGo Finance). It guided to $130bn, plus or minus 3%, for this quarter, which has an extra week and assumes no data-center sales to China. The stock closed down 0.44% at $155.46 before the report, then rose about 3.5% to $160.90 after hours; CoreWeave gained 4.7% and TSMC's US shares 5.1% (MLQ.ai). US futures rose about 0.5%.
calls.view: The beat settles the demand question for another quarter, and at RSI 23 before the report the stock was washed out, so a relief rally in chips is likely. It does not settle what drove the sell-off, how AI spending is financed at a 10-year yield above 5%, so the desk still expects AI spenders to lag steady earners through November, at medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes back above 26,000 before November 27.

calls.headline: Software leads a fourth S&P 500 fall as the Dow loses 849 points
calls.line: Salesforce fell 9.45% and ServiceNow 6.51% before Anthropic's listing.
calls.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, the Dow 1.64% to 50,759.42 and the Nasdaq 0.74%; every S&P sector fell and the VIX rose 11.1% to 25.46 (MLQ.ai, BigGo Finance). Salesforce lost 9.45% on reports of a new round of job cuts, ServiceNow 6.51% and Intuit 7.2%; the iShares software fund fell more than 3%. Oracle fell 3.4% to $115.00 and Microsoft 2.3% to $506.24. Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, as forecast.
calls.view: The fear of AI has moved from those spending on it to those it could replace: software sold off hardest on the eve of a listing that will raise up to $64.4bn for an AI developer. The desk expects software to keep lagging into Anthropic's first trades and Intuit's results on Thursday, at low confidence: the sector is already down sharply and a strong debut could lift AI names broadly.

calls.headline: Yields above 5% and a priced December hike push gold below $3,800
calls.line: The Fed's October minutes come out at 9pm Cairo time.
calls.body: Spot gold fell below $3,800 on Wednesday for the first time since September 30, 2025, as the dollar index stood near its highest since April 2025 and the 10-year Treasury yield held above 5% (Reuters via Yahoo Finance, BigGo Finance). Traders expect a quarter-point Fed hike in December, per CME FedWatch (Reuters via AOL). JPMorgan fell 2.4% to $329.96 with the market.
calls.view: Real yields this high are the main weight on gold and on long-duration stocks; the minutes can only add to it if they show more officials wanted to hike in October. The desk expects gold to stay under pressure while the 10-year holds above 5%, at medium confidence; banks gain on margins but not when the economy slows, so JPMorgan is mixed.
calls.wrong: Gold closes back above $4,000 before December 9.

calls.headline: Anthropic prices a listing of up to $64.4bn after the close
calls.line: The second-largest IPO on record starts trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday.
calls.body: Anthropic prices 825 million shares at $70–78 after the US close on Wednesday, which would raise $57.8bn to $64.4bn; it said in a November 17 filing it remains on track for that range (Reuters via Kitco, CoinMarketCap). Trading starts on the Nasdaq on Thursday.
calls.view: A deal this size draws money from other AI and software stocks in the days around it, which fits Tuesday's software selling; a strong first trade would also set a value for the AI developers that Alphabet and others hold stakes in. Low confidence on the direction: pricing at the top of the range is the signal to watch.

view.headline: Debt inflows and remittances keep the dollar in EGP 52–55
view.body: Sisi said on Tuesday the IMF program is nearly done, and Arab and foreign investors kept buying, $547m of debt on Monday and EGP 195m of shares on Tuesday, as Wall Street fell. With the one-year bill at 26.07%, record remittances and Brent down about 21% this month, the pound has room to hold near EGP 53–55 into the program's December 15 expiry. The risks are US 10-year yields above 5%, a half-point Fed hike and a delay to the final IMF review.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 before December 9, or a debt auction clears with bids below the amount offered.

notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram eased to EGP 6,745 on Tuesday and has yet to follow the ounce below $3,800.
notes.dxy: 103.60, near its highest since April 2025 on December hike bets; the pound held at EGP 53.80.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: about $64,500 on Wednesday morning, little changed.

news.headline: Gold falls below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025
news.text: The dollar near a 19-month high and a 10-year yield above 5% weigh on the metal.

news.headline: Brent settles at $93.14 as the IEA sees a supply surplus
news.text: Brent rose 0.76% on Tuesday; the IEA says October supply topped demand for the first time since the Iran war began.

news.headline: US jets strike a Revolutionary Guards site on Iran's Qeshm Island
news.text: The strike in the Strait of Hormuz came "in response to Iranian aggression," a US official said.

news.headline: Iran claims a strike on US Patriot systems in Kuwait
news.text: Iran's military said it hit Ali Al Salem air base early on Wednesday, its first claimed strike on a US base there in months.

news.headline: Dollar index hits a 19-month high on December hike bets
news.text: Traders expect a quarter-point Fed hike in December, with the US 10-year near 5.1%.
